name: Vegetable Pasty

ingredients.name: swede or turnip, peeled and finely diced

steps: Rub the cold cubed butter into the flour with your fingertips until coarse crumbs form. Mix in 4 g of the salt, then add the cold water a little at a time just until the dough holds together. Do not overwork it. Divide into four discs, wrap and chill for at least 30 minutes.

Cut the potato, swede, carrot and onion into small, roughly 5 mm dice so they cook through inside the pastry. Combine with green peas, the remaining 4 g salt and black pepper. Keep the filling raw and dry; drain thawed peas if using frozen ones.

Heat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray. Roll each chilled pastry disc into a circle about 20 cm wide and 3 mm thick. Divide the vegetable filling among one half of each circle, leaving a 2 cm border. Brush the border lightly with a little water, fold the empty half over and press into a D shape.

Crimp the curved edge firmly by folding and pressing small sections over one another. Put the four sealed pasties on the tray, cut a small steam vent in each top, and brush all exposed pastry with milk for an eggless finish. Chill for 10 minutes if the pastry has become soft.

Bake for 40–45 minutes until the crust is deeply golden and crisp and the potato and swede are tender when tested through a vent. If the crust colours too quickly, reduce the oven to 180°C for the final 10 minutes. Rest 10 minutes before serving; the vegetable filling will be very hot.
tips: This is a vegetable pasty, not a protected traditional Cornish pasty. Small, even vegetable dice are essential for cooking raw filling inside the folded pastry. The reviewed photo shows browned hand-crimped D-shaped pasties, one opened to reveal potato, swede, carrot, peas and onion.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
